outcome: A Windows machine with no Git or Python converges to a working harness by running 'forge doctor --fix' with zero typed setup: it adds a real Python 3.10+ check, installs Git and Python in user scope via winget, finds them through canonical known folders plus ProgramW6432 (WOW64-safe), and refreshes PATH so the fixing run reports green — or prints honest guidance when it cannot. forge.cmd lets cmd/PowerShell users run the harness natively and bootstraps Python before the Git Bash handoff. Auto-remediation refuses to run under an elevated shell (fail-closed), never executing user-writable installers as admin. New clients get it at init, existing on forge upgrade, and windows-latest CI proves it. The single-UAC elevation batch is deferred to real-Windows validation (D-0021).
